title: Hanseatic League
summary: The Hanse was an association of north European towns whose merchants dominated trade from London and Flanders to Scandinavia, the Baltic and Novgorod. In the twelfth century German merchants set up a trading centre at Visby on Gotland and soon founded Riga, Reval and Danzig; Lübeck replaced Visby as the League's centre in the thirteenth century and became its Queen City. Kontors at London, Bruges, Bergen and Novgorod handled cloth, furs and fish. Rivalries, stronger territorial states and Dutch competition brought decline in the sixteenth century.

uncertainty.note: No precise founding date (Encyclopedia.com); a commercial union of north German cities from 1241; Lübeck prospered until the 16th century (UNESCO), and the League declined in the 16th century.
